methodological_rigor.justification: Multicenter prospective cohort (CKCis) of 790 chRCC patients with surgically resected clinically localized disease (2011-2024). Median follow-up 4.9 years. Descriptive statistics, Kaplan-Meier curves with log-rank testing, Cox proportional hazards models. Appropriate statistical methods with FDR control. Limitations: prospective cohort without randomization; treatment heterogeneity; incomplete follow-up for some patients.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Prospective cohort study (LoE 2b) characterizing outcomes in surgically resected chRCC. Identifies prognostic factors for recurrence/survival in understudied chRCC subtype. Clinical utility demonstrated for risk stratification and patient counseling.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE-aligned observational cohort reporting: patient flow, baseline characteristics clearly presented, outcomes well-defined, statistical methods transparent. Large multi-institutional database (CKCis) enables robust analysis. Data availability: Canadian cohort registry with appropriate access governance.

novelty_literature.justification: Largest prospective chRCC outcomes study; identifies predictors of recurrence (pT stage, sarcomatoid features, positive margins, necrosis) and survival (pT stage, pathological size, age). Addresses literature gap in non-clear cell RCC understanding.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized prospective cohort report with clear clinical context establishing chRCC outcomes gap. Methods transparent. Results with Kaplan-Meier curves and risk factor tables clearly presented. Publication-ready structure.

key_strengths: Largest prospective multicenter chRCC cohort (n=790) with extended median 4.9-year follow-up enabling robust outcome assessment
Identifies clinically meaningful risk factors: pT stage, sarcomatoid features, positive margins, necrosis for recurrence; pT stage, size, age for survival
Demonstrates favorable outcomes for localized chRCC (93.6% recurrence-free at 5-yr, 94.5% OS at 5-yr) supporting optimal management approach
Prospective multicenter Canadian registry design reduces selection bias vs retrospective single-institution studies
key_concerns: Propensity score matching used but treatment heterogeneity across institutions not fully addressed; no adjustment for surgical approach differences (partial vs radical nephrectomy)
Limited follow-up for recurrence patterns: only 45 recurrences detected enabling detailed analysis
Outcomes highly favorable (93.6% RFS, 94.5% OS at 5-yr) may reflect selection toward good-prognosis disease or shorter follow-up in some cohort; generalizability to all chRCC populations unknown
chief_reviewer.rationale: High-quality prospective multicenter cohort study establishing favorable chRCC outcomes and identifying prognostic risk factors, supporting tier 3 for specialty journal publication following minor revisions.
